output.summary: REQ-019 needs one new event, product_comparison_viewed. It fires when the side-by-side compare table is shown with 2-4 products. It records the SKUs being compared so analysts can count compares and build co-comparison pairs and sets. No existing event covers comparing products. product_viewed should not be reused: it would inflate add_to_cart_rate. Whether add-to-cart can happen from the compare table is still open. If it can, product_added_to_cart will need a new source value, which would be an extend; that is not specced until Jon confirms.
clarifying_questions: Can users add a product to cart directly from the compare table? If so, I'll extend product_added_to_cart.source with a new allowed value 'compare'. Today those adds would fail validation or be mislabeled as 'pdp'.
Where can users start a compare: PLP/category grid, search results, PDP, or all of these? If you want compares broken down by entry point, I'll add an optional entry_point property with those values.
Is the compare table its own page (for example /compare) that fires page_viewed, or an overlay on the current page?

events.name: product_comparison_viewed
events.trigger: Fires once when the side-by-side compare table finishes rendering with 2-4 products. Fires again only if the user changes the set of products while on the table (adds, removes or swaps a product). Does not fire on re-renders, scrolls, resizes or toggling table rows. Must not also fire product_viewed for the products in the table.
events.description: User viewed a side-by-side comparison of 2-4 products. Used to count compares and to analyse which products are compared together.

properties.name: product_ids
properties.description: SKUs in the comparison, as an array of strings with 2-4 items. Order them in the column order shown, left to right. Analysts should sort the array before grouping into co-compared sets.

properties.name: product_count
properties.description: Number of products in the comparison; must equal the length of product_ids.

properties.name: category
properties.description: Product category, only when all compared products share one category; omit if they are mixed. Use the same values as product_viewed.category.

kpi_links.reason: The spec adds a new event and does not touch product_viewed or product_added_to_cart, so the KPI should not move. Two cases would change it. First, if engineering fires product_viewed for products shown in the compare table, the views denominator inflates. Second, if users can add to cart from the compare table, those adds are untagged or mis-sourced in product_added_to_cart until a 'compare' source value is added. Growth should confirm the KPI stays scoped to /p/* views.

If the compare table is its own page that fires page_viewed, it can add page views and sessions to this KPI's denominator. That effect is small and only matters if compare becomes a common landing or entry page.

output.privacy_notes: No personal data is needed. Send only SKUs, the product count and the category. Do not put user identifiers, emails or names in the event payload; rely on the standard anonymous or session identifiers your analytics SDK already attaches. If the compare page has a shareable URL, make sure page_path or referrer cannot carry user-entered text or account info in query strings.
